children.title: The keyboard
lines: ONE SAMPLE, every pad. Load a file and the whole keybed plays it,
higher or lower by which pad you press.
The pads are a keyboard: 32 pads, 32 notes, one semitone a pad, and
no two pads play the same note.
Pad 80 (second row out, fifth pad in) plays the sample at its own
speed. The bottom-left pad is an octave below it and the top-right
pad is nineteen semitones above; the pitch rises left to right,
bottom row first.
The Octave knob (Setup) moves the whole keyboard, one octave a step.
Move's own octave buttons move the pads' notes, and the keyboard
moves with them.

children.title: Loading a sample
lines: Samples page: Sample opens the browser. What you pick replaces the
sample the keybed is playing. There is only one.
The browser starts at /data/UserData/chompi-samples:
Built-in      the module's own wavs (the CHOMPI card set)
User Library  your own files, already on the Move
Copy WAV or AIFF files to User Library however you like; they show
up in the browser, and any rate, bit depth or channel count plays.
The pick is kept, and survives a reload of the chain. Clear puts
the keybed back on the built-in sample.

children.title: Tape, looper, recorder
lines: Tape: reverse, sustain, loop, attack, decay, start, end, gain,
pan. They shape the one sample, and they are remembered.
Looper: records the module's output into a 60 s buffer and plays
it back with pitch and dub. Loop Rec starts it, Loop Play starts
playback, Clear Loop empties it. Strt and End are the window the
loop turns over in; End below Strt plays that stretch backwards.
Recorder: Chompi Rec records the audio input (Input, In Gain).
Monitor passes the input through to the output. Move has one
output, so the line input is in the mix either way.
On load, every knob shows the value the sound is actually at.
Volume starts at 0.80, not at 0.
